text:
eva: Heads-up — nightly eval flagged a regression after canary deploy of v21b (weights + tokenizer update) against the 'long-form-reasoning' promptset. failure rate jumped from 4% -> 23%. samples look like truncated or repeated clauses.

nightly-bot: nightly-eval v21b-canary: 2026-03-19 03:12Z, suite=long-form-reasoning, fail_rate=23.1%, metric=coherence_drop, link=https://ci.internal/evals/2468101214

jon: ouch. any sample diffs? can you paste 1-2 bad generations vs baseline?

eva: pasted quick diffs below (baseline v20b float32 vs v21b-int4 canary):

```
PROMPT: "Summarize the rationale behind Keynesian fiscal stimulus during recessions."
BASELINE v20b-fp32:
"Keynes argued that during demand shortfalls, government spending can substitute for private consumption, stabilizing output and employment..."

CANARY v21b-int4:
"Keynes argued that during demand shortfalls, government spending can substitute for private consumption, stabilizing output and employment. government spending can substitute for private consumption. government spending can substitute for private consumption."
```

maya: that looks like degenerate repetition, possibly kv-cache misalignment or a decoding loop after tokenizer change. did token offsets shift?

liam: +1 on tokenizer offsets. v21b included new normalization that merges certain whitespace/punctuation. If decode/encode not symmetric with cached keys we can get wrong next-token logits.

sam: i pulled the tokenizer diffs — token ids reordered for a handful of punctuation merges ("--" -> en-dash mapping), and `lower_case_fold` tweak. but i didn't expect repetition. could be quantization amplifying marginal logits.

jon: let's triage: 1) reproduce generation with fp32 weights + v21b tokenizer 2) reproduce with v21b weights + v20b tokenizer 3) compare kv cache keys for same prompt. can someone run quick checks?

eva: running point 1 & 2 now on dev-gpu1. will dump kv prefix IDs and top logits.

nightly-bot: job started: reproduce-triage-2468101214 on dev-gpu1 (eva). ETA ~7m.

eva: interim logs — when using v21b weights + v20b tokenizer, repetition still appears but with lower intensity (fail rate ~12%). when using v20b weights + v21b tokenizer, failure ~9%. both worse than baseline 4%. suggests interaction between both changes.

liam: that points to combined effect. check whether kv cache indexing uses token lengths from tokenizer. if tokenizer now emits slightly different subtokens, past kv positions could be off by +/-1 leading to attention reading wrong cached keys.

eva: dumped kv IDs for prompt head (first 32 tokens) — here are first 8 ids v20b vs v21b:
```
v20b ids: [154, 2023, 11, 4021, 88, 7, 9012, 3]
v21b ids: [154, 2023, 11, 4021, 88, 7, 9012, 3]
```
They match for head, but later tokens diverge around punctuation near token 45.

sam: can you share the exact divergence spot and raw text? maybe a single merge changed alignment downstream.

eva: at char pos ~138: "...investment—especially in" v20b tokenized as ["investment", "—", "especially"]; v21b merged to ["investment—especially"] which then shifts downstream token indices.

jon: that explains cascading kv misreads. two possible mitigations: 1) switch to tokenizer compatibility mode (legacy split) for the canary 2) flush kv cache after punctuation merges for live sessions 3) patch runtime to use absolute position keys rather than token index relative positions.

maya: quick win: flip on tokenizer legacy normalization for canary and re-run nightly. we should push a hotfix to disable merge for now.

liam: agree. also run a weight-only diff: compare v20b -> v21b float32 (no quant) to see if weights alone create any degenerate loops. quant might amplify but not originate.

eva: i've run the float32 weight-only check overnight earlier — small uptick in incoherence (4% -> 6%), so weights contribute but minor. tokenizer change is larger contributor.

sam: creating canary rollback branch: revert tokenizer merges but keep weight changes. deploying to canary pool now.

nightly-bot: deploy canary branch (tokenizer-compat-mode) started: job=deploy-2468101214-compat, targets=canary-gpu-*.

jon: once deployed, run a 2-hour eval sweep and post aggregated metric table. if fail_rate returns to ~5% we keep weight changes and iterate tokenizer patch.

eva: noted — queued eval run. also capturing anchor promptset where repetition is most common (legalqa + econ-longform). will add those to regression monitors.

maya: FYI, add unit test to decoder that checks for tokenization symmetry between encode(decode(encode(x))) for edge punctuation cases. should catch this earlier.

liam: and file a follow-up to consider robust kv indexing using character positions for boundary-sensitive attach points.

eva: thanks all. i'll post the eval link and a short postmortem if rollback fixes it. :thumbsup:

nightly-bot: eval-complete: canary-tokenizer-compat-mode run finished, suite=long-form-reasoning, fail_rate=5.2%, link=https://ci.internal/evals/2468101214/compat

jon: great signal. re-enable canary traffic policy to 50% while we craft tokenizer patch.

sam: raised PR with tokenizer compat toggle + unit tests: https://git.internal/r/s/3321 (putting it behind a runtime flag).

eva: merging and coordinating staged rollout. closing triage for now, will reopen if new patterns appear.
